newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Tajik government seeks to regain key military base.
newsitem.headline: Tajik government seeks to regain key military base.

text.p: Tajik government troops clashed on Thursday with Islamist opposition guerrillas who captured a strategic base at the village of Sagirdasht in the Pamir mountains, Tajik Defence Ministry sources said.
"The opposition have Sagirdasht and they are trying to take the surrounding heights," one source told Reuters.

Sagirdasht, situated in the Tavildara region 200 km (120 miles) east of the Tajik capital Dushanbe, is strategically important because it has facilities for helicopters to land troops and supplies in the remote, mountainous area.
The region straddles the only road between government- controlled territory in the west and the mountainous eastern half of the country largely controlled by opposition guerrillas.
"Government forces are taking defensive action," the source said.
The fighting contravenes a much flouted United Nations-sponsored ceasefire.
Abdullo Kodiri, an opposition official with the Dushanbe-based U.N. commission monitoring the ceasefire, confirmed Sagirdasht was taken by opposition forces on Saturday.
"Sagirdasht is under the control of opposition fighters," Kodiri said.

The four-year civil war between the government and opposition guerrillas has cost tens of thousands of lives and displaced many more. Thousands of refugees live in dust-blown camps in neighbouring Afghanistan.
